summary.intent: Conduct a security review of the feat/store-ipns-crypto-data-in-db branch (IPNS signature/pubkey storage in DB), fix all identified vulnerabilities, and merge via PR.
summary.outcome: Security review completed with 8 findings (2 HIGH, 3 MEDIUM, 3 LOW); all HIGH/MEDIUM issues fixed and pushed to PR #448, though a tsup build config regression (noExternal bundling Node builtins into ESM) caused a desktop build failure that required a follow-up fix splitting CJS/ESM configs.

repo: @cipherbox/crypto depends on ESM-only packages (@libp2p/crypto, @noble/ed25519, @noble/hashes, ipns) that cannot be require()'d by NestJS (CommonJS) or Jest without bundling them into the CJS output.
The API (NestJS) runs in CommonJS; the desktop/web apps use Vite which handles ESM externals itself — so @cipherbox/crypto needs separate CJS (fully bundled) and ESM (externals kept) outputs.

IPNS names are cryptographically derived from the public key via deriveIpnsName(); without binding pubKey→ipnsName on resolve, a server can substitute its own keypair and the client accepts the forged record.
The web app (apps/web/src/services/ipns.service.ts) was not sending publicKey on publish, making the server-side and client-side signature verification dead code for web-published records.

code.finding: Must use two separate defineConfig entries: CJS with noExternal: [/.*/ ] to bundle all ESM-only deps, and ESM without noExternal so Vite can resolve browser-compatible versions. Using clean: true only on CJS (first) entry prevents wiping the CJS output when ESM builds.
resolveIpnsRecord verified signature validity but never bound pubKey to ipnsName — needed deriveIpnsName() check after signature verification to prevent key substitution attacks.
Used spread operator for base64 encoding (String.fromCharCode(...bytes)) which causes call-stack overflow on large records; also was not deriving or sending publicKey on publish.
MaxLength(100) on publicKey field but a 32-byte key base64-encodes to 44 chars — MaxLength should be 70 (with padding headroom). Applied to both PublishIpnsDto and PublishIpnsEntryDto.
deriveEd25519PublicKey lacked input validation; added check that private key is exactly 32 bytes before passing to noble/ed25519.

workflow: When fixing an ESM/CJS compatibility issue, verify the fix doesn't break other consumers (Vite-based browser builds) before pushing to CI.
Always do a full local pnpm build before pushing dependency/build-config changes to CI.
Start the API locally (even without all services) to confirm require() of new dependencies works before pushing.
Security review workflow: identify → parallel false-positive filter → fix → update report with RESOLVED status → commit report and fixes separately.

friction: 1Password SSH signing agent caused a transient commit failure that required a retry.

Two CI iterations wasted on the ESM-only bundling issue: first iteration only bundled @libp2p/* but missed @noble/* and ipns; second used noExternal: [/.*/ ] which broke Vite by bundling Node builtins into ESM output.
The full build was not run locally before pushing the noExternal fix, which would have caught the Vite regression immediately.
CI log fetching via gh CLI required multiple attempts to locate the actual error message.
open_items: Finding #4 (signature verification downgrade — server can omit signature fields and signatureVerified returns false but callers never check it) was deferred as a design decision; callers should be audited to enforce signatureVerified === true.
Finding #5 (inconsistent key zeroization in crypto functions) was deferred as a convention issue rather than fixed.
The tsup config split fix (CJS bundled, ESM external) was committed but the commit failed due to 1Password SSH agent error at end of session — needs verification that it was actually pushed.
